rationale: Interpret receipt 8502c21215334cbc81e6b277849a7d1d, the second run of the transfer flag window, and refine one sentence the earlier reading got wrong. The repeat again returned an empty transfer error in 0 ms with the transfer flag clear before the call and the named demoted member never leading, so all three transfer harnesses now have two runs. Its single case did differ from the first run in where leadership ended, and the leader-loop code shows why that difference does not make the first reading safe: the future is answered nil when the leader leaves office, while the in-progress flag is set and reset on the leader-loop goroutine, so a caller sampling the flag after the call and a 10 ms state sampler can each miss the stepdown, the reset, or a same-node re-election. The counterevidence sentence that treated the clean first call as evidence the transfer did not run is therefore replaced, the three-harness limitation now reads as two runs per harness, and the joint history records the repeat. The repeat is cited in the account text and joint history rather than added to the recorded execution set, whose one entry belongs to the interpretation's own experiment identifier. The conclusion and the scoped defect claim are unchanged: the request is admitted without a suffrage check and never installs the named member.

interpretations.rationale:
Conclusion: violated, and the scoped defect is asserted. A leadership transfer that explicitly names a member the configuration marks as a non-voter is admitted without any refusal keyed to its suffrage and does not install that member as leader; the attempt instead forces an election round in which every member's term advances, leadership lands on a member the caller did not name, and leadership is absent for a measurable interval in the earlier five-member receipts, while the four-member receipt below recorded no leaderless sample. Evidence, five receipts of the same experiment lineage. Parsed index 1 of receipt d436029b08c5425aa5aec577901cb8ba and of successor receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f, the control where the explicit target is an ordinary voter: target_ever_leader=true, final_leader_is_target=true, future_ok=true, target_term_after=3 with other_member_term_max_after=3, so the mechanism installs the named target with a single term advance. Parsed index 3 of both receipts, the trigger where one non-leader member was demoted with DemoteVoter before the transfer: future_ok=true with an empty future_error, target_ever_leader=false, final_leader_is_target=false, target_term_after=4 and other_member_term_max_after=4, while the case event (parsed index 2) records target_demoted=true and transfer_target_role=nonvoter. A successor run, receipt 4185f1615cf54e4fbd4801044480416d, corrects the earlier measurement: the target's own configuration is read after DemoteVoter returns and polled until it changes (demotion_converged=true, demotion_converge_ms=0), and at the moment the transfer is requested the target itself reports target_role_in_own_config=nonvoter, so the member's own view already showed it held no vote; it still campaigned (7 candidate samples, 7 leaderless samples, target_term_after=4, target_ever_leader=false, future_ok=true with an empty error) while the voter control at parsed index 1 installed the named target and produced 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples. In receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f the trigger produced 8 candidate samples with 8 leaderless samples (about 80 ms with no member reporting Leader) out of 470 samples at roughly 10 ms spacing, against 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples out of 471 in that run's control. The two cases differ only in the target's suffrage, so the outcome difference is attributable to eligibility, not to the transfer path, harness or transport timing. Mechanism from source: leaderLoop resolves an explicit id only through leaderState.replState (raft.go:687-742), which startStopReplication populates for every configured server including non-voters, whereas the automatic path's pickServer skips non-voters outright (raft.go:2186-2206); leadershipTransfer replicates the target and sends TimeoutNow (raft.go:991-1023), and timeoutNow (raft.go:2232-2237) marks the receiver as a leadership-transfer candidate with no suffrage, term, leader or membership check; electSelf raises the target's term and asks every voter, whose requestVote handler adopts the higher term and steps down before rejecting the non-voter (raft.go:1696-1707). The trigger's term pattern (target and all other members at 4, one step beyond the rejected round) and its leaderless interval match exactly that path, while the control's single-step advance to 3 matches a successful transfer. Clean-copy repeat, receipt 3324fe87d6da49c6b53eab0e116823df (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): re-executing the corrected experiment from its retained inputs reproduced the pair. Parsed index 0, the voter control: target_role_in_own_config=voter, future_ok=true in 2 ms, target_ever_leader=true, final_leader_is_target=true, and 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples out of 471. Parsed index 2, the trigger case: target_demoted=true, demotion_converged=true at 0 ms and target_role_in_own_config=nonvoter; parsed index 3: future_ok=true with an empty error in 2 ms, target_ever_leader=false, final_leader_is_target=false, 6 candidate samples and 6 leaderless samples (about 60 ms) out of 470, target_term_after=4 and other_member_term_max_after=4. The corrected result is therefore observed twice with the target's own configuration confirming the non-voter role at request time. Demotion race, receipt 62e8b8bdcc9f448687b6588dda84125d (twenty attempts, each on a fresh four-voter cluster): the harness started DemoteVoter for a follower and immediately issued LeadershipTransferToServer for the same member, without waiting for the demotion to commit or for any voter to apply it. Parsed index 1 records demote_ok_count=20, transfer_ok_count=20, target_led_count=0, final_target_count=0 and target_ended_nonvoter=20, with no transfer error. Issuing the two requests back to back therefore cannot install a member whose vote is being removed: the transfer is admitted and reports success, and the election it provokes is still rejected because the voters' applied configuration decides the outcome. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a caller that names a serving but non-voting member receives a completed transfer with no error, no transfer of authority, an extra election round that raises every member's term, and a leaderless interval whose length follows the configured election timeout.

Entry-point comparison, receipt a319426e86514f45b2053a7b3bd8050b (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): one four-member cluster per case, one follower demoted in each, and the demoted member's own configuration view reporting the non-voter role before the transfer, converging in 0 ms in the control and 6 ms in the trigger. Parsed index 0 records the control's state and parsed index 1 its result: the automatic LeadershipTransfer() needed one attempt, its future returned nil in 106 ms, leadership ended on a voter that is not the demoted member, no leaderless sample was seen in 26 samples over three seconds, and a client Apply and a GetConfiguration afterwards both succeeded. Parsed index 2 records the trigger's state and parsed index 3 its result: five attempts spanning 1035 ms each returned 'leadership transfer in progress', the named member never reported Leader across the same 26 samples, the final leader is a different voter, and the client Apply and GetConfiguration afterwards both succeeded. The control therefore shows that transfer works on this cluster shape and that the automatic path avoids the demoted member, while the explicit path admits the named member, keeps reporting a transfer in progress, and never installs it; both the earlier nil futures and this receipt's in-progress errors are consistent with the same gap, since neither is a refusal keyed to the target's lack of a vote.

Transfer-state probe, receipt 78769a572c5b4b249e441ac7ce63422a (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): the same demote-then-transfer setup run twice with the leader's leadership-transfer flag sampled around each call. Parsed index 0 records the single-case state and parsed index 1 its result: the flag read false before the call, false as soon as the future was returned, false after the future completed and false three hundred milliseconds later; one attempt completed in 0 ms with no error, the named member never reported Leader across 283 samples over three seconds, no sample was leaderless, and the final leader is a different member. Parsed index 2 records the retry-case state and parsed index 3 its result: the flag read false before the first attempt, that attempt returned no error so the loop stopped after one, the named member never led across 284 samples, six samples were leaderless (about 60 ms), and the final leader is again a different member. Two things follow. The request was issued with no transfer already running and the library nevertheless accepted the demoted member as a target and reported the transfer as complete, so the earlier receipt's in-progress error is not evidence of a pre-existing transfer; and because the future succeeds while the named member never leads, the surface the caller sees is success, not a refusal, which is the form of the gap the account claims.

Repeat of the entry-point comparison, receipt e023eecf02c74f4db5bc8c5a16fd3586 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): the same fixed inputs were run again with no changes. Parsed index 0 records the control's state and parsed index 1 its result: one automatic attempt completed in 106 ms with no error, leadership ended on a voter that is not the demoted member, no leaderless sample was seen in 26 samples, and a client Apply and GetConfiguration afterwards both succeeded in about 2 ms. Parsed index 2 records the trigger's state and parsed index 3 its result: the first attempt already returned 'leadership transfer in progress', all five attempts over 1036 ms returned the same error, the named member never reported Leader, the final leader is a different voter, and the post-transfer Apply and GetConfiguration both succeeded. The in-progress surface therefore reproduces exactly in this harness across two runs, with the same error, the same five attempts and the same roughly one-second span, so it is a stable property of this sequence rather than a one-off event; the flag probe's clean first call remains a different sequence, and the difference between them is not yet identified.

Repeat of the demotion race, receipt 334d7a88f3b244548f316bcdb42b779e (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): the same randomised loop of twenty attempts ran again. Parsed index 0 records the case with four members and twenty attempts, and parsed index 1 its result: twenty demotions succeeded, twenty transfer futures completed with an empty last error, the named member led in none of the attempts, no attempt ended with it leading, and it ended as a non-voter in all twenty. The nil-future surface is therefore reproducible in this harness across two runs, alongside the entry-point harness's reproducible in-progress surface and the flag probe's single clean call, so the account now holds two independently reproduced futures outcomes for the same request rather than one of each.

Repeat of the flag-window probe, receipt 8502c21215334cbc81e6b277849a7d1d (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): the third harness ran again from its retained inputs. Parsed index 0 records the single-attempt case's state and parsed index 1 its result: the leader's transfer flag read false before the call and false at every later sample, the one explicit request completed with an empty error in 0 ms, the named member never reported Leader, no leaderless sample appeared in 283 samples, and leadership ended on the same voter it began on. Parsed index 2 records the retry case's state and parsed index 3 its result: the flag again read false before the first attempt, that attempt returned an empty error in 0 ms, six leaderless samples appeared over 283, leadership ended on a voter that is not the named member, and the named member never led. The nil future therefore reproduces in this harness across two runs, and each of the three harnesses now has two runs of the same request.

The two flag-probe runs differ in one respect that the code explains, and the difference corrects how the earlier 0 ms nil should be read. The future is answered nil on the leader-loop path that closes when the leader leaves office, where the code logs 'lost leadership during transfer (expected)', and on the completed path whose doneCh carries no error (raft.go:687-742, raft.go:745-762), so a nil result in 0 ms means the leader relinquished leadership immediately rather than that the request was refused. The in-progress flag is set inside the leader loop after it receives the request and is reset by the goroutine's deferred call (raft.go:727, raft.go:783), with the source itself noting the window in which a caller may observe the request in flight after its future has been answered. A flag read immediately after the call, and a 10 ms state sampler, can therefore both miss a stepdown and a reset. In the first run the single case ended on a different voter than it began on; in this run it ended on the same voter with zero leaderless samples, which is what a stepdown followed by an immediate re-election of the same node looks like to that sampler. Neither run is evidence that the transfer did not run, and neither run installed the named member.
counterevidence: The documentation's promise is soft rather than a guarantee: it says it is 'very likely' the target wins and that a follower which cannot be promoted 'will fail gracefully' (api.go:1296-1330), and the leaderLoop code deliberately reports nil with the message 'lost leadership during transfer (expected)', which can be read as the future reporting only that leadership was relinquished. The claim therefore rests on the admission of an ineligible target and on the observed outcome, not on the future's wording alone.

The control cases show the same mechanism transferring leadership correctly: the explicit transfer to an ordinary voter installed that named voter with a single term advance, and the later automatic control completed in about a hundred milliseconds with leadership on a voter and no leaderless samples. The defect is therefore specific to the eligibility of an explicitly named target, not to leadership transfer in general or to the entry-point harness's sequencing.

The measured disruption is small in absolute terms because the cluster ran with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms): the three trigger runs recorded 8, 7 and 6 leaderless samples (about 80, 70 and 60 ms) and one extra election round, against zero leaderless samples in the voter controls. The interval follows the configured election timeout, so a production configuration of about 1 s would scale it accordingly; these millisecond figures are not a bound for other settings.

No committed entry was lost, no vote was counted for an ineligible candidate, and no decision-safety property was contradicted in either case; what is contradicted is the completion signal and the authority outcome of the explicit transfer.

Both corrected runs show the target's own configuration had already converged to non-voter before the request, so the exercised case is a member that knew it could not win; a demoted member whose own view still lagged (a stale configuration) was not exercised, although the earliest runs exercised an unknown mix.

The demotion race is a negative result for elevation: in 20 attempts issued back to back, no target became leader and every transfer reported success, so the timing gap that could have produced a worse outcome did not do so in this harness.

The future's result is not uniform across receipts: the demotion race receipt 62e8b8bdcc9f448687b6588dda84125d recorded successful transfer futures in all twenty attempts, while receipt a319426e86514f45b2053a7b3bd8050b recorded 'leadership transfer in progress' on every one of five attempts on a four-member cluster whose demoted member's view had already converged. The sentence that the future completes without error therefore describes those receipts and not the operation in general, and the durable observation common to both is that the named member is never installed and no suffrage check refuses it. The repeat of the entry-point comparison, receipt e023eecf02c74f4db5bc8c5a16fd3586, reproduced the in-progress surface exactly, with the same error on all five attempts over 1036 ms, so within that harness the surface is stable. A second run of the demotion race, receipt 334d7a88f3b244548f316bcdb42b779e, reproduced that surface, with twenty successful futures and no attempt in which the named member led.

The in-progress error seen in receipt a319426e86514f45b2053a7b3bd8050b is not reproduced in the flag probe: with the transfer flag reading false before the call, the explicit request returned an empty error in 0 ms in both of its runs, receipts 78769a572c5b4b249e441ac7ce63422a and 8502c21215334cbc81e6b277849a7d1d. The account therefore cannot claim that the error is a stable consequence of naming a non-voter, only that neither outcome is a refusal keyed to the target's suffrage and neither installs the target. The 0 ms nil is itself weak evidence of anything but relinquishment: the future is answered nil when the leader leaves office or when the transfer goroutine reports no error, and the flag is set and reset on the leader-loop goroutine, so a caller sampling the flag right after the call, or a 10 ms state sampler, can miss both the stepdown and the reset. The two flag-probe runs illustrate this: the first ended on a different voter than it began on, the second on the same voter with zero leaderless samples, which a same-node re-election would also produce.
limitations: The cluster size is four members throughout, with three voters after the demotion, and the transfer always targets a non-leader member. The demotion race covers a transfer issued concurrently with the demotion, but a cluster whose only non-voter is the sole reachable member and a transfer that lands while the leader is already losing office to another election were not tested.

Leaderless counts are sampled every ~10 ms over roughly 4.7 s of the 5 s window (470 to 471 samples); a gap shorter than the sample spacing would be missed, so 60 to 80 ms is a lower bound for the trigger and the controls' zero does not prove uninterrupted leadership.

Only immediate convergence was observed in the corrected runs: the demoted member's own view reported the new role within the first poll (0 ms), so no single-case run exercised a target whose configuration still showed it as a voter at request time. The demotion race issues the transfer before applying, but it records the target's final role rather than its view at request time.
That the voter members had committed the demotion before the transfer is inferred from their rejection and term adoption, not from reading each voter's configuration.

Out of scope: whether an unprivileged or misconfigured peer could send TimeoutNow directly, even though timeoutNow performs no term, leader or membership check (raft.go:2232-2237); that path was not exercised here.

Three harnesses now give a reproduced futures outcome on two runs each for the same request: the demotion race returned successful futures in all twenty attempts on both of its runs, the entry-point harness returned 'leadership transfer in progress' on all five attempts on both of its runs, and the flag probe returned an empty error in 0 ms with the flag clear before the call on both of its runs, receipts 78769a572c5b4b249e441ac7ce63422a and 8502c21215334cbc81e6b277849a7d1d. The difference between the flag probe and the other two therefore lies in their preceding steps, which include repeated leader and configuration polling before the transfer, and which of those steps sets the transfer state is not yet identified; all three keep the demoted member's own view reporting the non-voter role before the call. Within the flag probe the futures surface reproduced while the observable disruption did not: the single case ended on a different voter in the first run and on the same voter with zero leaderless samples in the second, so the 10 ms sampler cannot separate a same-node re-election from a transfer that never caused a stepdown.
interpretations.joint_history: All five receipts belong to this investigation. Receipts d436029b08c5425aa5aec577901cb8ba, 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f and 4185f1615cf54e4fbd4801044480416d are successive revisions of the same fixed experiment: the first run, a revision adding per-member state sampling, and the revision that reads the target's own configuration after the demotion. Receipt 3324fe87d6da49c6b53eab0e116823df is a clean-copy repeat of the third revision executed from its retained inputs, with identical case names, admissions and assertions. Receipt 62e8b8bdcc9f448687b6588dda84125d comes from a separate experiment identifier, cf5136d55dd74f22ad66c73229d55f35-experiment, which keeps the same demote-then-transfer sequence but starts both requests back to back on a fresh cluster per attempt and summarises twenty attempts; it intervenes on the same mechanism under the same question, and its outcome is compatible with the single-case receipts. Receipt a319426e86514f45b2053a7b3bd8050b comes from a further experiment identifier, 6f0e1da8cb8048f5b28060a73243fa6b-experiment, which keeps the same demote-then-transfer shape and adds an automatic-transfer control on the same four-member cluster shape plus a client write after the transfer attempt. Receipt 78769a572c5b4b249e441ac7ce63422a comes from a further experiment identifier, 2690c8dadb9c4631b3fe90d9626cadb9-experiment, which keeps the demote-then-transfer setup and adds sampling of the leader's transfer flag around the call, so the earlier receipt's in-progress error can be attributed rather than assumed. Receipt e023eecf02c74f4db5bc8c5a16fd3586 is a repeat execution of 6f0e1da8cb8048f5b28060a73243fa6b-experiment from its retained inputs, so its cases, admissions and assertions match receipt a319426e86514f45b2053a7b3bd8050b. Receipt 334d7a88f3b244548f316bcdb42b779e is a repeat execution of cf5136d55dd74f22ad66c73229d55f35-experiment from its retained inputs, so its case, admissions and assertions match receipt 62e8b8bdcc9f448687b6588dda84125d. Receipt 8502c21215334cbc81e6b277849a7d1d is a repeat execution of 2690c8dadb9c4631b3fe90d9626cadb9-experiment from its retained inputs, so its two cases, admissions and assertions match receipt 78769a572c5b4b249e441ac7ce63422a.
